jobs.title: Environmental Remediation Engineer/Scientist/Geologist
jobs.description:
At Jacobs, we're challenging today to reinvent tomorrow by solving the world's most critical problems for thriving cities, resilient environments, mission-critical outcomes, operational advancement, scientific discovery and cutting-edge manufacturing, turning abstract ideas into realities that transform the world for good.

Your impact

We’re seeking an environmental geologist/engineer/scientist with a background in environmental site characterization and remediation to support the delivery of challenging projects for government and global private sector clients.

Based out of the Sacramento or Oakland, California area, you’ll work with other scientists, engineers, subject matter experts, and project managers on exciting projects in which you will learn from others and pass along your knowledge. Responsibilities may include designing, performing, or overseeing soil, soil vapor, groundwater, and surface water investigations, working among teams of colleagues and subcontractors, coordinating and managing fieldwork logistics, data analysis and interpretation, and technical report writing. You'll work alongside recognized technical experts, developing and implementing comprehensive site strategies, and delivering innovative solutions for some of our most challenging site issues.

Projects require thoughtful strategy development, leveraging technical expertise, and collaboration with clients and stakeholders. All projects must be delivered with the high safety, compliance, and quality standards expected by both Jacobs and our client. Our global team is here to provide you with the tools and support needed to grow your skills and career, as well as those of your colleagues. By driving consistency and innovation across projects, you'll help your team achieve client goals. Bring your positive attitude and strong, collaborative style, and together, we'll tackle complex environmental remediation challenges and solve our client’s problems.

At Jacobs, we’re partnering across the globe to create the best project outcomes by maximizing the design, digital technology, and support capabilities of our Global Integrated Delivery (GID) teammates. By joining Jacobs, you’ll commit to supporting and engaging with these teams, as we work to build a company like no other.

This is a position located near the Sacramento or Oakland office in Northern California, with flexibility to work from home, the nearby Jacobs office, and project sites to meet project delivery goals while maintaining balance.

Here's what you'll need

Bachelor's degree in Geology, Environmental Science, Environmental Engineering or other closely related science field or other closely related field
At least 2 years of experience delivering environmental site characterization and remediation projects in the industry, including fieldwork methodology/procedures and assessment/evaluation of data for various environmental media (e.g., soil, groundwater, sediments)
Experience conducting environmental remediation site investigation field work, working on project sites, and overseeing subcontractors
Experience working with multi-disciplinary teams toward a common goal
40-hr HAZWOPER certification or the ability to attain this certification
Effective verbal and written communication skills with coworkers and contractors
Strong attention to detail when conducting field work and evaluating data

Our health and welfare benefits are designed to invest in you, and in the things you care about. Your health. Your well-being. Your security. Your future. Employees have access to medical, dental, vision, and basic life insurance, a 401(k) plan, and the ability to purchase company stock at a discount. Eligible employees may also enroll in a deferred compensation plan or the Executive Deferral Plan. Jacobs has an unlimited U.S. Personalized Paid Time Off (PPTO) policy for full-time salaried/exempt employees, seven paid holidays, and caregiver leave. And certain roles may be eligible for additional rewards, including merit increases, performance discretionary bonus, and stock.

The base salary range for this position is $66,300.00 to $100,210.00. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional factors, including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. Job posted on July 22, 2026. This position will be open for at least 3 days.

We value collaboration and believe that in-person interactions are crucial for both our culture and client delivery. We empower employees with our hybrid working policy, allowing them to split their work week between Jacobs offices/projects and remote locations enabling them to deliver their best work.

Your application experience is important to us, and we’re keen to adapt to make every interaction even better. If you require further support or reasonable adjustments with regards to the recruitment process (for example, you require the application form in a different format), please contact the team via Careers Support.

jobs.title: Technical Solutions Engineer
jobs.description:
About Artos

At Artos, we build tools that help biopharma companies create and manage their R&D documentation in a fraction of the time. If you’re looking to join a team whose mission is to fundamentally change the way that drug development gets done, we’d love to talk to you.

The Role

We're looking for a Technical Solutions Engineer to bridge the gap between engineering and customer success.

This is a deeply technical, customer-facing engineering role. You'll become the primary technical contact for customers deploying Artos both via our cloud and in BYOC contexts, helping them successfully install, configure, troubleshoot, and scale the platform. You'll investigate complex technical issues, diagnose problems down to root cause, and work closely with our engineering team to resolve them.

You'll also own much of the technical documentation our customers rely on—from deployment guides and architecture documentation to engineering responses for security and compliance reviews.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys debugging distributed systems as much as working directly with customers. You'll spend your time solving real technical problems rather than routing tickets, and you'll have significant ownership over the customer experience.

What You'll Do

Own customer technical success

Serve as the primary technical point of contact for customers deploying Artos into their own cloud environments.
Help customers configure infrastructure, permissions, networking, authentication, and other deployment requirements.
Investigate and resolve technical issues that arise during implementation and production usage.
Diagnose customer-reported issues by tracing behavior from symptoms through logs, infrastructure, and application code to identify root causes.
Escalate and partner with engineering when product changes or deeper investigation are required.

Build and maintain technical documentation

Own customer-facing technical documentation, including deployment guides, architecture references, integration documentation, and troubleshooting resources.
Create and maintain engineering documentation required for customer security reviews, compliance questionnaires, and technical due diligence.
Continuously improve documentation based on customer feedback and recurring support patterns.

Collaborate across engineering and customer teams

Partner closely with engineering to reproduce issues, validate fixes, and improve product reliability.
Work alongside Forward Deployed Engineers on larger or more complex customer implementations.
Collaborate with Implementation and Customer Success teammates to translate customer needs into technical solutions.
Identify recurring customer challenges and help improve the product, tooling, and deployment experience.

What We're Looking For

Strong software engineering fundamentals with experience debugging production systems.
Experience deploying or supporting cloud-native applications on AWS, Azure, or GCP.
Comfort working with containers, networking, authentication, IAM, APIs, and modern infrastructure.
Excellent troubleshooting skills, with the ability to independently isolate complex technical issues.
Strong written communication skills with experience creating technical documentation.
Ability to communicate effectively with both engineers and non-technical stakeholders.
A bias toward ownership, curiosity, and solving customer problems end-to-end.

Nice to Have

Experience supporting enterprise SaaS customers.
Familiarity with Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, or infrastructure-as-code.
Experience responding to enterprise security questionnaires or compliance reviews.
Experience supporting BYOC or self-hosted enterprise deployments.
Familiarity with AI/LLM infrastructure or modern ML platforms.

Other Information

Very comfortable working in a fast-paced and intense startup environment

Willing to work in-person in our office in Mission Bay 4-5 days/week

Likes matcha KitKats, believes every LLM prompt is just Schrödinger’s cat waiting to be observed, and knows too many random facts about the Mongol postal system

Compensation Range: $166.5K - $231K

ITASCA North America is seeking a Senior Hydrogeologist/Groundwater Modeler to support challenging groundwater, mine water, and environmental projects across the U.S. and North America.

Strong experience developing, calibrating, applying, and interpreting numerical groundwater models.

Strongly valued

Mining industry experience, particularly mine dewatering, depressurization, pit inflow, pore-pressure estimation, water balance, closure, groundwater recovery, or operational hydrogeology.

Sanmina Corporation has facilities strategically located in key regions throughout the world.

Industrial Engineer/Project Coordinator

Job Purpose

Our Houston facility is looking for a practical, highly organized Industrial Engineer / Project Coordinator
to join our team during a major plant expansion. In this role, you will work directly with our Facilities Manager to coordinate equipment installations, track project timelines, and manage vendor schedules.

Because we are expanding, you will also act as a flexible engineering resource to help our Process and Manufacturing Engineers when workloads are high. Beyond physical facility coordination, this role focuses heavily on data analysis—tracking manufacturing costs, calculating floor efficiency, and identifying operational waste. This is an excellent opportunity to gain hands-on experience in facility planning, factory software systems, financial tracking, and project management.

Nature Of Duties

Track Equipment Installations: Work directly with equipment suppliers and contractors on the plant floor. Monitor delivery schedules, ensure utilities (power, air, etc.) are ready for setup, and track installation progress.
Manage Factory Software & Data: Use Oracle ERP and our Manufacturing Execution System (MES) to enter production routes, audit labor hours, and keep our manufacturing data accurate.
Conduct Time Studies & Costing: Spend time on the production floor timing assembly steps to compute cycle times. Use this data to help accounting establish accurate standard labor and machine costs.
Track Waste & Rework Costs: Collect and analyze data on scrap rates, material waste, and rework labor hours. Investigate the root causes of these variances to help the team reduce lost profitability on the floor.
Analyze Equipment Downtime & Capacity: Monitor machine utilization metrics through the MES. Categorize why machines stop (maintenance delays, slow setups, or waiting on parts) to help improve overall capacity.
Map Workflows & Material Flow: Create clear process flowcharts and value stream maps (VSM) using Microsoft Visio. Analyze material handling paths and operator travel times to minimize transit costs and prevent product damage.
Create Status Reports & Decks: Gather project updates, capacity metrics, and financial variance data to build clear, professional PowerPoint presentations for our management team and our customers.
Support Engineering Changes: Help the engineering team manage Engineering Change Notices (ECN), update risk assessments (PFMEA), and write simple, clear standard operating procedures (SOPs) for operators.

Bachelor’s Degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a similar technical field.
0–3 years of experience in a manufacturing or heavy assembly plant (internships or co-op experience count).
Basic understanding of manufacturing cost structures, labor routing steps, material waste tracking, and cost variances (standard vs. actual).
Ability to work well with different people, from shop-floor operators to external contractors and senior managers
Able to explain technical updates, project delays, and financial data clearly, both out loud and in writing.
Comfortable changing priorities quickly to help out where the plant needs it most.
